title: Upload an image for a catalog item

claims.text: The PicController exposes an endpoint at /Pic/UploadImage that accepts an HTTP POST request.
The endpoint requires an image file named 'HelpSectionImages' and a 'itemId' from the request form.
The system checks if the uploaded image is valid based on its format (JPEG, PNG, or GIF).
If the image is valid, it is uploaded temporarily using the IImageService, and a JSON object containing the image's path and URL is returned.
The upload endpoint expects an image file via the 'HelpSectionImages' field and a catalog item ID via the 'itemId' field in the form data.
If the image is not valid, the system returns an HTTP 400 Bad Request with the message 'image is not valid'.
If the image is valid, the system calls _imageService.UploadTempImage to upload the image temporarily and obtain a URL.
Upon successful upload, the system returns a JSON object containing the image's path and URL.
The UploadImage action endpoint expects a file named 'HelpSectionImages' and a form field 'itemId'.
Image files must be in JPEG, PNG, or GIF format to be considered valid.
If the image is not valid, the system returns an HTTP 400 Bad Request status with the message 'image is not valid'.
The system uploads the image temporarily using the IImageService, passing the image file and the catalog item ID.
Upon successful temporary upload, the system returns a JSON object containing the image's path and URL derived from the temporary URL.

title: Upload an image for a Catalog Item

claims.text: The system provides a web service endpoint to upload an image, expecting the file to be sent under the field name 'HelpSectionImages'.
The upload process requires an 'itemId' to associate the image with a catalog item.
The system validates the uploaded image format to ensure it is one of JPEG, PNG, or GIF.
If the image validation fails, the service returns an HTTP 400 status code indicating the image is not valid.
Upon successful validation, the service calls the IImageService to upload the image temporarily, associating it with the catalog item ID, and returns the resulting image URL and name as JSON.
